title: Moving source refs during long deploys are not deploy failures
summary: Agents may treat a moving branch name or mutable image tag as if it stayed fixed for a long build or deploy. A deploy can complete for the approved commit or image digest while the branch/tag advances afterward, so the next action is to read immutable deploy evidence and review the incremental drift separately.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid reusing approval for newly merged code, mislabeling a successful frozen-SHA deploy as failed, or bypassing reviewed deployment paths when branch heads or tags move during long rollouts.

contexts: a deploy, build, or rollout starts from a branch name, symbolic git ref, workflow ref, or mutable container image tag
the build or rollout is long enough that commits can merge or tags can move before completion evidence is checked
review or approval applies to one commit/image, but the agent observes a newer branch head or tag after rollout
the deploy system records immutable evidence such as commit SHA, image digest, release manifest, task definition revision, deployment id, or smoke result

tools.name: amazon-ecs
tools.version_range: ECS service deployments using image tags/digests; docs checked 2026-05-08
observed_versions: AWS ECS software version consistency docs current on 2026-05-08

trigger_signals.description: The deploy uses a branch, symbolic ref, or workflow ref but also records a specific expected commit SHA.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat the commit SHA as the immutable deploy target for this batch; the branch name is only a moving selector unless separately pinned.

trigger_signals.description: The branch head observed after rollout differs from the deployed or approved commit.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Do not mark the frozen deploy as failed solely because the branch advanced. Open an incremental review for the difference.

trigger_signals.description: A rerun or manual workflow dispatch defaults to the current branch head instead of the originally approved commit.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Confirm the rerun target SHA before assuming it is the same reviewed artifact or commit.

trigger_signals.description: The deployment uses a mutable container image tag while the platform or registry can resolve an immutable digest.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Read the image digest or deployment artifact identity before reasoning from the tag name alone.

trigger_signals.description: A deployment packet describes one reviewed pull request or release candidate, but the target branch now contains newer commits.
trigger_signals.pattern: target branch advanced|new commits after review|unexpected high-risk files|reviewed PR differs from deploy target
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat the deployment scope as the exact target commit, not the remembered PR or branch name. Rebuild the packet for the actual target before deploying.

trigger_signals.description: Review packet generation, CI waits, or deploy preparation took long enough for the remote target ref to move.
trigger_signals.pattern: remote target differs|review packet stale|merge-base changed|ref moved before gate
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Fetch and compare the remote target immediately before the expensive gate; stale review evidence does not authorize the moved ref.

negative_signals.description: The deploy target was an immutable commit SHA, signed release, immutable tag, or image digest, and no newer target is being considered.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: If both approval and deployment are pinned to the same immutable identity and no moving selector is used for follow-up, this trap may not apply. Continue normal deploy verification.

negative_signals.description: The post-rollout evidence shows the deployed artifact itself is unhealthy or differs from the frozen deploy record.
negative_signals.pattern: smoke failed|health check failed|artifact digest mismatch|task failed|rollback
negative_signals.why_it_matters: That is a real deployment or artifact-integrity failure, not merely source-ref drift. Diagnose the failed rollout directly.

negative_signals.description: The human or release policy explicitly approved the later commit range after it was reviewed separately.
negative_signals.pattern: incremental range reviewed|approved new SHA|separate review complete
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A later SHA can be deployed safely after its own review. The trap is reusing the earlier approval without checking the drift.

common_wrong_assumptions: The branch head after deploy is what production must be running.
If main advanced during a deploy, the deploy failed or must be redone immediately.
Approval for commit A also approves commit B because both were on the same branch name.
A container image tag such as latest identifies one stable artifact.
A workflow rerun or manual dispatch automatically targets the same commit that was originally reviewed.
Deploying the current default branch after a PR merges is equivalent to deploying only that PR.
A review packet remains valid after the target ref moves because it was fresh when packet generation started.

first_checks.check: Read immutable deployment evidence: deployed commit, image digest, release manifest, task definition or deployment id, rollout state, and smoke result.
first_checks.why: Production truth should come from the deploy record and artifact identity, not the moving branch or tag observed afterward.
files: container registry or task definition output

first_checks.check: Compare the deployed immutable identity with the current branch head or current tag digest.
first_checks.why: This separates a completed frozen deploy from a new, unreviewed incremental change.

first_checks.check: Inspect only the incremental range for gated changes before treating catch-up as simple.
first_checks.why: New commits may include DB, security, permission, billing, or public-behavior changes requiring independent review.

first_checks.check: For workflow reruns or manual dispatch, confirm the exact target SHA and artifact identity before redeploying.
first_checks.why: A rerun path may use the current branch head or supplied ref, which can differ from the earlier reviewed commit.

first_checks.check: Immediately before review or deployment, fetch the remote target ref and compare it with the commit named in the review packet.
first_checks.why: This catches scope drift introduced by merges that landed while CI, packet generation, or deployment preparation was running.
first_checks.command: git fetch <remote> <target-ref> && git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD && git merge-base --is-ancestor <reviewed-sha> FETCH_HEAD

first_checks.check: Inventory the incremental range for high-risk paths before treating catch-up as routine.
first_checks.why: New commits may add migrations, schema changes, permissions, billing paths, or publication/security work that require a separate gate.

decision_rules.condition: Deploy evidence shows the approved deploy SHA or digest reached steady state and smoke checks passed, while the branch head or tag moved afterward.
decision_rules.then: Treat the frozen deploy batch as complete for its immutable target. Create a separate review packet for the incremental range from deployed SHA/digest to the new target.

decision_rules.condition: The agent is about to rerun or manually dispatch a deploy from a branch name after earlier approval was tied to a specific SHA.
decision_rules.then: Check the workflow run target ref and SHA. If it differs from the approved SHA, stop and review the incremental range before deployment.

decision_rules.condition: A mutable image tag is used in task definitions or deployment config, but the platform exposes a resolved image digest.
decision_rules.then: Compare and record the image digest used for the deployment. Do not infer artifact identity from the tag alone.

decision_rules.condition: The incremental range includes database migrations, permissions, auth/security, billing, publication, destructive history/data operations, or other hard-gated changes.
decision_rules.then: Do not catch up automatically. Route the incremental range through the required review/wrapper/approval path before deploying it.

decision_rules.condition: The target ref moved after review or after a PR merge and the incremental range has not been reviewed.
decision_rules.then: Stop the expensive gate, rebuild the review/deploy packet for the current target commit, and route any high-risk expansion through the required path.

do_not: Do not reuse approval for commit A to deploy newly merged commit B.
Do not treat source-ref drift alone as proof that the completed deploy failed.
Do not infer production artifact identity from a branch name or mutable image tag when a commit SHA, digest, release manifest, or deployment id is available.
Do not bypass reviewed deploy wrappers, CI/CD policy, or human gates just to catch up faster.
Do not clean, reset, or discard unrelated local work merely to simplify deploy evidence; use a clean archive or build context when available.
Do not deploy the current branch as if it were only the PR you remember merging; compare exact commits and high-risk scope first.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Read immutable deploy evidence, fetch and compare the target ref immediately before gates, then close the frozen batch or rebuild the review/deploy packet for any moved scope.

risk.notes: Deployment can affect live availability, billing, permissions, auth/security, data, and public behavior. This record supports diagnosis and review partitioning; it does not authorize production deployment or catch-up.

title: Evidence gates should distinguish not applicable from missing
summary: A safety gate creates alarm fatigue when it blocks on absent evidence for a risk class whose trigger files or operations are absent from the current change.
ai_value: Helps agents design gates that remain strict for real risk surfaces while emitting auditable not-applicable evidence for out-of-scope classes.

contexts: review, deploy, migration, release, or policy gates require evidence artifacts
different evidence classes apply only to certain files, operations, or risk surfaces
review packets need to show why skipped evidence was safe to skip

trigger_signals.description: The gate reports missing evidence for a class whose trigger files or operations are absent.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Emit not_applicable with the trigger check result instead of a noisy blocker.

trigger_signals.description: Reviewers learn to bypass or ignore the gate because low-risk changes repeatedly fail on irrelevant requirements.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: False blockers erode the gate's authority for real risk.

trigger_signals.description: The review packet does not show how the agent proved an evidence class was out of scope.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Skipped classes still need auditable proof of absence.

negative_signals.description: The trigger check is unavailable, partial, ambiguous, or could not be evaluated.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not claim not_applicable without a trustworthy trigger check; fail closed.

negative_signals.description: The change might touch live data, schema, credentials, permissions, billing, production availability, or irreversible state.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: High-risk uncertainty requires evidence or authorized narrowing, not a skip.

common_wrong_assumptions: Every absent evidence artifact is equally missing.
A human can infer from the diff why a gate was skipped.
False blockers are harmless because reviewers can bypass them.

first_checks.check: Define trigger conditions for each evidence class before checking for the evidence artifact.
first_checks.why: The trigger is what separates missing from not applicable.

first_checks.check: For every skipped class, emit a machine-readable not_applicable record with the trigger command/check and result.
first_checks.why: Future reviewers need proof of absence, not silence.

first_checks.check: Test three fixtures: trigger present with evidence, trigger present without evidence, and trigger absent.
first_checks.why: The third fixture protects against alarm-fatigue false blockers.

decision_rules.condition: Trigger conditions are absent and the trigger check is complete and trustworthy.
decision_rules.then: Emit not_applicable with the check and result, include it in the review packet, and do not block on the absent artifact.

decision_rules.condition: Trigger conditions are present or the trigger check cannot be evaluated.
decision_rules.then: Treat missing evidence as a blocker until the evidence is supplied or an authorized reviewer narrows the scope.

do_not: Do not use not_applicable when the trigger check is unavailable, partial, or ambiguous.
Do not weaken gates for live data, schema, credentials, permissions, billing, availability, or irreversible state.
Do not hide skipped evidence classes from the review packet.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Define evidence triggers, emit auditable not_applicable records when triggers are absent, and fail closed when triggers are present or uncertain.

title: A null optional endpoint may be a route convention, not a missing contract
summary: When a response omits an optional endpoint URL, the intended contract may be that clients derive a fixed route from a base URL. Check the convention before changing server output or widening the API envelope.
ai_value: Helps agents repair client/server integration failures on the correct side of the contract instead of turning an intentional null field into an unnecessary server behavior change.

contexts: an API envelope includes a nullable or optional endpoint field
client code has enough base metadata to derive a stable route
documentation, route constants, or older clients define a fixed path convention elsewhere

trigger_signals.description: The response has a null or absent endpoint field but includes a base URL, tenant URL, origin, or other stable route base.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Investigate whether the endpoint is intentionally derived client-side.

trigger_signals.description: Existing clients or docs construct the same route from constants and a base URL.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat the null field as part of the contract until tests prove otherwise.

negative_signals.description: The route path is tenant-specific, permission-specific, or otherwise cannot be derived from stable public metadata.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Server-provided endpoint data may be necessary; do not assume derivation.

negative_signals.description: Contract documentation requires a non-null endpoint and clients do not contain a derivation fallback.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The missing field may be a real server-side contract violation.

common_wrong_assumptions: A null endpoint field always means the server forgot to send data.
Adding another URL field is safer than reading existing client route conventions.
A client-side fix is wrong if the failing response contains null.

first_checks.check: Search client constants, route helpers, tests, and docs for the same endpoint path.
first_checks.why: This separates an intentional fixed-path convention from a missing server contract.

first_checks.check: Add or run a client test with the optional endpoint set to null or omitted.
first_checks.why: The test should prove whether the client derives the reviewed route without server changes.

first_checks.check: Document the derivation rule beside the client code that applies it.
first_checks.why: Future agents need to know the null field is not automatically a missing contract.

decision_rules.condition: A stable route convention exists and the envelope carries enough base metadata.
decision_rules.then: Keep the server contract unchanged and make the client derive the fixed route through the established helper.

decision_rules.condition: No stable derivation rule exists or the path varies by data the client cannot know.
decision_rules.then: Review the API contract and add server/client tests before changing either side.

do_not: Do not widen an API envelope solely because an optional endpoint is null.
Do not duplicate route strings in multiple clients instead of using the established helper.
Do not hide a missing-contract problem by inventing a derivation rule after the fact.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Look for a fixed route convention and test null-endpoint handling before changing server response shape.

risk.notes: Client-side tests and documentation are low risk; changing public API contracts may require normal review.

title: Operational queues need wake-one and backup paths
summary: Adding a wait queue around a shared operational choke point is not enough. The queue needs FIFO no-overtake, wake-one handoff, backup retry, and a strict wait-is-not-authorization boundary.
ai_value: Helps agents prevent queue stampedes, skipped waiters, stuck heads, and accidental permission bypasses in multi-agent operations.

contexts: multiple agents wait for a shared lane, lock, deploy slot, review slot, or other operational choke point
a wrapper adds waiting around a resource but not queue discipline
authorization or hard-gate checks are separate from resource availability

trigger_signals.description: Many waiters wake at once when one holder releases the resource.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Use wake-one handoff rather than broadcast wakeups to avoid stampedes.

trigger_signals.description: A later waiter can overtake the head of the queue after release.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Preserve FIFO order or record an explicit priority override.

trigger_signals.description: The queue head can be missed or remain stuck after a lost notification.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Add a timer or heartbeat backup path that rechecks safely without tight polling.

trigger_signals.description: A waiter treats reaching the front of the queue as permission to perform a gated action.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Separate resource availability from authorization; the hard gate still applies.

negative_signals.description: Only one actor can ever use the resource and no wait state is exposed.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A queue may add needless state; a simple lock can be enough.

negative_signals.description: The action is hard-gated and authorization is absent.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Queue position cannot grant permission; stop until the real gate is satisfied.

common_wrong_assumptions: A lock with wait messages is automatically fair.
Waking all waiters is safer because someone will proceed.
If I am first in queue, I am authorized to act.

first_checks.check: Test the queue with at least three waiters and one release.
first_checks.why: This exposes overtakes and broadcast stampedes.

first_checks.check: Simulate a lost wakeup or stale holder and verify the backup timer wakes exactly the head or reports a safe wait.
first_checks.why: Queue systems need a mercy path that is not tight polling.

first_checks.check: Assert that gate checks still run after a waiter becomes eligible.
first_checks.why: Resource availability and authorization are separate state machines.

decision_rules.condition: Release wakes multiple independent waiters.
decision_rules.then: Wake only the next eligible waiter and record the handoff evidence.

decision_rules.condition: Queue state can overtake or lose the head.
decision_rules.then: Store ordered wait state and add a bounded timer or heartbeat recheck for lost wakeups.

decision_rules.condition: The next waiter lacks the action authorization.
decision_rules.then: Keep or release the resource safely, but do not perform the gated action until authorization is separately satisfied.

do_not: Do not broadcast wake all waiters for a single shared resource release.
Do not let queue position override hard gates, review requirements, or owner decisions.
Do not tight-poll a queue when a heartbeat or scheduled backup recheck is enough.
Do not use queue discipline as a substitute for choosing the right lock target; cross-check lock-shared-resource-not-artifact for resource-vs-artifact lock scope.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before adding wait behavior to a shared operational resource, test FIFO order, wake-one release, lost-wakeup recovery, and separate authorization checks.

title: Preserve orphan work before cleanup
summary: When edits or commits are found outside the expected branch, owner, or session, preserve and classify them before cleanup. Only clearly agent-owned, local, reversible partial state should be narrowly reverted or neutralized.
ai_value: Helps agents recover from branch drift, abandoned sessions, and dirty worktrees without destroying useful edits or asking a human to classify raw Git state.

contexts: a worktree is dirty after a session crash, branch movement, or handoff
commits or edits exist outside the expected branch or task
cleanup pressure appears before ownership and purpose are known

trigger_signals.description: Git status shows uncommitted changes, untracked files, or detached commits that the current task did not create.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat them as evidence to preserve, not clutter to erase.

trigger_signals.description: The parent branch moved and local edits no longer apply cleanly.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Capture the diff and purpose before deciding whether to split, rebase, or discard.

negative_signals.description: The files are generated artifacts proven reproducible and ignored by policy.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: They may be regenerated or cleaned through normal repo rules.

negative_signals.description: A reviewed destructive cleanup path has already classified the work as disposable.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Follow that path, preserving the classification evidence.

common_wrong_assumptions: A clean worktree is always safer than preserving unknown changes.
Untracked files are probably junk.
The human should choose from raw branch labels instead of the agent classifying purpose and risk.

first_checks.check: Capture the status, diff summary, and likely purpose in a safe artifact.
first_checks.why: A later reviewer needs evidence even if the session that made the edits is gone.

first_checks.check: Classify ownership: current task, sibling task, generated residue, or unknown.
first_checks.why: Classification decides whether to adopt, split, preserve, or ignore.

first_checks.check: Only clean or discard after the classification is recorded and the applicable gate passes.
first_checks.why: Destructive cleanup without classification loses recovery options.

decision_rules.condition: Unknown edits exist in a shared or task worktree.
decision_rules.then: Save a patch or evidence summary, identify likely owner/purpose, and defer destructive cleanup until classification is recorded.

decision_rules.condition: The unknown edits may contain secrets or private data.
decision_rules.then: Do not publish the diff; preserve privately and use the appropriate confidentiality path.

decision_rules.condition: The partial state is clearly agent-owned, local, reversible, and inside the approved scope.
decision_rules.then: Prefer a narrow revert or neutralization that returns the scope to a known-safe state; preserve and report anything with unknown ownership, evidence value, or protected effects.

do_not: Do not reset, delete, or overwrite unknown edits to make status look clean.
Do not paste potentially private diffs into public records or broad chats.
Do not ask a human to choose from raw implementation labels when the agent can classify evidence.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Capture status and diff evidence, classify ownership and purpose, then clean only through a recorded safe path.

title: High-stakes incident probes should safe-halt at the approval boundary
summary: When an agent investigating a high-stakes data or operations incident reaches live data, destructive recovery, deployment, permission, publication, or other irreversible boundaries, the correct next deliverable is often a safe halt with evidence rather than an improvised fix.
ai_value: Helps autonomous agents preserve trust during urgent investigations by distinguishing read-only or reversible probe work from actions that require a fresh owner, maintainer, or independent-review gate.

contexts: an agent is debugging a production, production-like, or customer-impacting data-system inconsistency
a probe starts read-only or dry-run but uncovers database rows, rollback steps, deployments, access changes, publication, billing, or irreversible recovery actions
multiple infrastructure layers appear relevant and the agent is tempted to keep fixing the next layer without rechecking authorization
an orchestrator or reviewer must decide whether the next action is still inside the approved probe scope

trigger_signals.description: The task begins as a read-only, dry-run, rollback-probe, or consistency investigation but the next tempting action would change live state or external visibility.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Classify the next action before running it; a mutation or visibility change is not automatically covered by probe authorization.

trigger_signals.description: The agent has enough partial evidence to explain a likely fault but not enough authorization to mutate live data, deploy, publish, or perform recovery.
trigger_signals.pattern: likely root cause|evidence points|probably fixed by|just run|apply rollback|make live
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Evidence can justify a handoff or approval request; it does not by itself grant authority for irreversible action.

trigger_signals.description: Several infrastructure layers surface in sequence, such as application behavior, persistent state, automation wrappers, operational preflights, and review or rollback tooling.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Map layers and apply narrow fixes only within the currently approved effect boundary; do not treat adjacent layers as implicit approval expansion.

trigger_signals.description: A long-running diagnostic is silent or nearly silent, making observers uncertain whether it is stuck, safe, or crossing a boundary.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Emit safe progress breadcrumbs so humans and other agents can decide whether to wait, review, or stop without guessing.

trigger_signals.description: The same approval is being stretched from one target class or operation class to a related but not explicitly approved target or operation.
trigger_signals.pattern: same issue|related target|adjacent|also fix|while here|same approval
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat target-set or operation-class expansion as a new scope decision unless the original gate explicitly covered it.

negative_signals.description: The task is purely local, synthetic, disposable, and has no live data, external visibility, credentialed systems, destructive operation, or irreversible effect.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Normal reversible coding and testing can continue when no high-stakes boundary is present.

negative_signals.description: A reviewed runbook or explicit owner/maintainer decision already grants the exact live mutation, target set, and recovery action being taken.
negative_signals.pattern: approved live runbook|explicit approval|exact target set|reviewed rollback|authorized mutation
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The trap is unauthorized boundary expansion, not execution of a precise reviewed live action.

negative_signals.description: The agent is only drafting a de-identified retrospective, candidate lesson, or local handoff and is not touching live systems or external publication paths.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Drafting generic learning artifacts can be safe when sensitive details and publication gates are respected.

negative_signals.description: The next action is read-only and explicitly inside the approved target class and operation class.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The correct response may be to continue the narrow probe while preserving evidence and progress logs.

common_wrong_assumptions: Emergency context means the agent may keep escalating until the system is fixed.
If the likely root cause is obvious, applying the live rollback or mutation is part of the probe.
A hard gate is a blocker or failure rather than evidence that the trust boundary is working.
Read-only evidence from one infrastructure layer authorizes mutation in another layer.
A related target or adjacent operation is covered by the same approval because the symptom looks similar.
Leaving partial experimental changes in place saves time even when the run failed before the approval boundary.

first_checks.check: Restate the approved scope in generic terms: environment class, target class, allowed operation class, and explicit non-goals.
first_checks.why: Scope language prevents discovery momentum from turning into unapproved mutation or target expansion.

first_checks.check: Classify the next step as read-only, reversible local change, generated artifact, live mutation, destructive operation, publication or access change, or irreversible recovery.
first_checks.why: The classification determines whether the agent can proceed, needs independent review, or must ask for a gate.

first_checks.check: For diagnostics that may run long enough to look stalled, emit short progress breadcrumbs with phase, safety class, and next gate.
first_checks.why: Progress logs let other agents and humans decide whether to wait, stop, or review without resorting to unsafe guesses.

first_checks.check: Keep a scratch evidence log separate from the live recovery action: observed evidence, checks run, assumptions, and the exact decision still needed.
first_checks.why: A separate evidence log preserves progress without converting investigation notes into unapproved execution.

first_checks.check: When multiple infrastructure layers surface, map them without crossing layers automatically: symptom, persistent state, automation behavior, review gate, and owner or business decision.
first_checks.why: Layer mapping supports narrow fixes while avoiding the false inference that one layer's evidence authorizes every adjacent fix.

first_checks.check: Before writing code, records, or public artifacts, check the working tree and preserve unrelated dirty files.
first_checks.why: High-stakes incidents often leave many artifacts; publication or code fixes must not mix unrelated local work.

decision_rules.condition: The next action is read-only and inside the approved target class and operation class.
decision_rules.then: Run the diagnostic, emit a brief phase/progress line if it may look stalled, and preserve evidence for the handoff.

decision_rules.condition: The next action is local-only and reversible, such as drafting a handoff, review packet, or public-safe candidate lesson.
decision_rules.then: Check the working tree, modify only scoped artifacts, avoid sensitive identifiers, and route publication or canonical promotion through an independent review gate.

decision_rules.condition: The next action would mutate live data, deploy, apply schema changes, change access or publication, incur material cost, or perform irreversible recovery.
decision_rules.then: Stop before mutation and produce the smallest approval request containing evidence, uncertainty, scope, and the default-safe state.

decision_rules.condition: The agent is unsure whether the next action is read-only, reversible, live, destructive, publication-related, or irreversible.
decision_rules.then: Do not run the action while ambiguous. Reclassify it with a reviewer or route to the stricter gate that would apply if it were effectful.

decision_rules.condition: The investigation has multiple active AI participants or touches high-risk operational boundaries.
decision_rules.then: Have one agent author the probe or handoff and a different agent review the scope, boundary, evidence, and redaction before risky next steps or publication.

do_not: Do not mutate live databases, apply migrations, deploy, publish, change permissions, incur material cost, or trigger irreversible recovery under probe-only approval.
Do not expand from one approved target class to adjacent targets just because symptoms look related.

Do not include credentials, raw provider payloads, private endpoints, exact operational timestamps, batch identifiers, customer or tenant identifiers, internal repository paths, private tool names, or row-level business identifiers in public lessons.
Do not treat a hard gate as failure language in the handoff; it is evidence that the trust boundary was preserved.
Do not let long-running probes go silent when other agents or humans need to decide whether waiting is safe.
Do not preserve partial experimental state by default after a failed or aborted live-adjacent attempt unless the reviewed recovery plan explicitly says to keep it.
Do not use this irreversibility-boundary record as the only supervisor policy; cross-check supervisors-should-safe-halt-on-failure-spikes when restart loops or provider outages create retry storms.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: At the first live, destructive, publication, access, cost, or irreversible boundary, stop before effectful action and produce a scoped evidence handoff; continue only with exact review or owner authorization for that boundary.

risk.notes: This record concerns high-stakes operational boundaries. It should make agents more conservative about effectful actions, not more confident to self-authorize them.

sources.supports: Independent redaction review found the source lesson public-safe and approved publication with non-blocking polish notes that were reflected in the canonical record.

title: Progress artifacts must be visible from the runtime that displays them
summary: A progress UI or status API can look blank even while a job is running if it reads a local artifact path that exists only on the agent/operator host and not inside the production runtime serving the UI.
ai_value: Before wiring a progress page to files, logs, or run-state artifacts, agents should prove that the display runtime can read the same source, or add a durable bridge such as a database row, object-storage object, or service endpoint.

contexts: long-running imports, backfills, syncs, or batch jobs that write progress to local files or logs
a web UI, API, dashboard, or alerting path runs in a different container, VM, account, or host from the job owner
agents are asked to make progress visible without interrupting the running job

trigger_signals.description: The progress source path starts with a local workspace, temp directory, or operator-host path while the display code runs in a remote production or preview runtime.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Check runtime visibility before debugging the UI component itself.

trigger_signals.description: A local script can read current progress, but the deployed page or API returns blank, null, not found, or an old snapshot.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Suspect a visibility boundary between job artifacts and display runtime.

trigger_signals.description: The requested fix explicitly says not to stop, restart, or mutate the running job.
trigger_signals.pattern: do not stop|do not restart|read-only|running job|live import
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Use a read-only bridge or snapshot path; do not 'fix' visibility by moving or restarting the owner process without authorization.

negative_signals.description: The job owner and display runtime share the same durable mounted volume with documented read permissions and lifecycle.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A file source can be valid when runtime visibility is explicitly designed and verified.

negative_signals.description: The display path intentionally shows only persisted terminal summaries, not live progress.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A blank live-progress card may be expected if the product does not promise live status.

negative_signals.description: The deployed API can read the artifact source in the target runtime but still returns wrong values.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then the defect is more likely parsing, auth, tenant selection, caching, or rendering rather than artifact visibility.

common_wrong_assumptions: If an agent can read a progress file locally, the production UI can read it too.
A blank progress page means the job is not running or the React component is broken.
The quickest visibility fix is to restart the job inside the web runtime.
Sidecar bridges are permanent architecture rather than temporary operational adapters unless explicitly retired.

first_checks.check: Name the job owner runtime and the display runtime, then prove whether the progress source exists inside both.
first_checks.why: The source must be visible from the reader, not only from the writer or the agent shell.

first_checks.check: Smoke the deployed status API and compare it with a read-only local progress read.
first_checks.why: A mismatch distinguishes display-runtime visibility from job progress itself.

first_checks.check: If a bridge is added, record its owner, cadence, connection count, stop condition, and retirement path.
first_checks.why: A temporary sidecar can solve visibility without becoming invisible production coupling.

decision_rules.condition: The progress artifact is local to the job host and invisible to the display runtime.
decision_rules.then: Publish read-only progress through a durable shared channel such as a database snapshot, object-storage object, or small service endpoint; avoid restarting or relocating the live job unless separately authorized.

decision_rules.condition: A temporary bridge is used to preserve a live job and meet an urgent visibility need.
decision_rules.then: Document the bridge process, update cadence, resource use, stop condition, and the future direct-write design that will retire it.

do_not: Do not assume local filesystem artifacts are available to a remote or containerized display runtime.
Do not stop or restart a live job merely to move its progress writer closer to the UI unless the operation is authorized.
Do not leave a temporary progress bridge without a named owner, stop condition, and retirement path.
Do not include private service names, internal URLs, tenant identifiers, account identifiers, repository paths, or organization-specific tool names in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: When a progress UI is blank but local run-state exists, first prove runtime visibility of the progress source; then bridge through a shared durable channel if needed.

risk.notes: Candidate is based on one private operational case. It should be reviewed and de-identified again before promotion, especially around live database, process, or production mutations.

sources.supports: A live import wrote progress to a host-local run-state artifact while the production web runtime could not see that path; a database snapshot bridge made the production progress card visible without stopping the import.

title: Quoted heredocs prevent accidental report execution
summary: When writing Markdown, reports, or scripts through a shell heredoc, quote the terminator. Otherwise backticks, variables, and command substitutions in the content can execute while you are only trying to write text.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid turning harmless-looking documentation or handoff text into accidental shell execution, file corruption, or secret exposure.

contexts: an agent writes Markdown, JSON, shell snippets, or handoff reports via heredoc
the content includes backticks, dollar signs, command substitutions, or examples of shell commands
the file being written will be trusted as evidence or instructions

trigger_signals.description: A heredoc delimiter is unquoted while the body contains backticks, `$()` or shell variables.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Assume the shell may expand or execute content before it reaches the file.

trigger_signals.description: A generated report contains missing code spans, unexpected output, or substituted values.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Re-read the file and check whether heredoc expansion occurred.

trigger_signals.description: An unquoted heredoc executed a command while the agent was trying to write a report, and the command was gated or potentially mutating.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Stop and treat this as a gate-crossing incident, not merely a formatting mistake.

negative_signals.description: The heredoc body is deliberately intended to expand variables and the values are safe.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then document that intent and avoid secret-bearing content.

negative_signals.description: A non-shell file writer or safe templating library is used instead.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The heredoc-specific trap does not apply.

common_wrong_assumptions: Markdown code spans inside heredocs are inert.
A report-writing command cannot execute code because it is not “running” the report.
If the command succeeded, the file content must be what was intended.

first_checks.check: Use a quoted terminator such as `<<'EOF'` for literal content.
first_checks.why: This disables shell expansion inside the heredoc body.

first_checks.check: Re-read the file after writing.
first_checks.why: Verification catches accidental expansion, truncation, and formatting damage.

first_checks.check: Avoid placing secrets or destructive commands inside executable shell heredocs.
first_checks.why: If quoting is wrong, sensitive content or commands can leak or run.

decision_rules.condition: A heredoc writes literal documentation, reports, or examples.
decision_rules.then: Quote the delimiter, write the file, then re-read the result before claiming the artifact exists.

decision_rules.condition: The heredoc already ran unquoted with shell syntax inside.
decision_rules.then: Inspect the resulting file and shell output, then rewrite through a quoted delimiter or safer writer.

decision_rules.condition: An unquoted heredoc executed a gated or potentially mutating command.
decision_rules.then: Stop; verify state with read-only checks; do not reflexively roll back destructively; record the incident; route the next gated action explicitly.

do_not: Do not use unquoted heredocs for literal Markdown containing backticks or `$()` examples.
Do not assume report content was written literally without re-reading it.
Do not include secret-bearing examples in a shell-expanded heredoc.
Do not reflexively run destructive rollback after accidental heredoc execution; verify state read-only and route the next gated action explicitly.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Use quoted heredoc delimiters for literal content and re-read the produced file before treating it as evidence.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified. It does not authorize bypassing human, maintainer, security, publication, billing, data, or credential gates.

sources.excerpt: AI recovery guidance identified unquoted heredocs containing shell syntax as a recurring report-writing hazard.
sources.supports: Supports the quote-and-reread publication record.

title: Release must cover all ownership layers
summary: A closeout helper that releases one visible lock does not prove the workspace is free. Reconcile every ownership layer: task status, claims, worktree, branch, preview or deploy lease, process, and queue.
ai_value: Helps agents finish multi-layer work without leaving hidden residue that blocks or misleads the next worker.

contexts: a multi-agent workflow uses several coordination layers such as task trackers, file/path claims, branches, worktrees, preview environments, deploy leases, background processes, or review queues
a cleanup helper reports success for one layer
the next worker may reuse a surface after closeout

trigger_signals.description: A finish or release helper reports success but read-only inventory still shows claimed paths, held locks, active sessions, worktrees, or serving leases.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat closeout as incomplete until every task-owned layer is resolved or intentionally held.

trigger_signals.description: A branch is deleted but the worktree remains, or a worktree is removed but the task or claim remains active.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Release operations are not necessarily cascading across layers.

trigger_signals.description: A helper refuses a specific scope and the agent silently skips that layer.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Record the refusal and use the narrow owner-supported fallback rather than hiding the gap.

negative_signals.description: The project has a single canonical ownership layer and inventory proves no other layers exist.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A full layered checklist would be unnecessary ceremony.

negative_signals.description: A remaining hold is intentionally kept for a documented hard gate or verification window.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Intentional holds are not residue when holder, reason, and release condition are recorded.

negative_signals.description: The leftover artifact is standing infrastructure rather than a per-task workspace.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not delete shared infrastructure while clearing per-task residue.

common_wrong_assumptions: One successful release command means all claims are released.
Session ended means file, environment, and deploy locks are gone.
The layer just touched is the only layer that matters.
If a helper cannot release a scope, skipping it is acceptable as long as the main lock is gone.

first_checks.check: List workflow ownership layers before cleanup: task status, session, file/path claims, preview/deploy lease, branch, worktree, process, queue, and source-of-truth record.
first_checks.why: Agents otherwise anchor on the layer they just touched.

first_checks.check: Release each task-owned layer through its owning helper or documented narrow fallback.
first_checks.why: Different helpers often have different scopes and do not cascade.

first_checks.check: Re-run read-only inventory after release and compare against the task scope.
first_checks.why: Post-release inventory distinguishes clean closeout from hidden residue.

decision_rules.condition: One ownership layer released but inventory still shows task-owned residue.
decision_rules.then: Do not report the workspace free. Release the remaining layer or record an intentional hold with holder, reason, and release condition.

decision_rules.condition: A helper refuses the requested release scope and a narrower supported release path exists.
decision_rules.then: Use the narrower helper, record the refusal, and leave process feedback for wrapper improvement.

do_not: Do not report all claims released based only on one successful command.
Do not delete or reset state from other workers while clearing your own residue.
Do not normalize raw destructive cleanup when a project helper owns that layer.
Do not hide helper gaps from the closeout report.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: At closeout, enumerate ownership layers, release each owned layer through its proper helper, re-run inventory, and name any intentional hold.

risk.notes: This record is about coordination hygiene. It does not authorize force-releasing other workers, destructive cleanup, or bypassing hard-gated holds.

sources.supports: Final six-candidate review preserved disagreement: Gemini favored standalone publication; Claude favored merging into session-boundary reconciliation. Codex selected standalone because the layered-release checklist is sharper than the broad session-boundary record.

title: Release source is not merge source
summary: A reviewed feature being ready to merge does not authorize deploying the current integration branch head. Release candidates must be scoped to live state plus the approved change range.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid shipping unrelated branch-head work while performing closeout, publication, or deploy steps for one approved change.

contexts: an integration branch has advanced beyond the reviewed feature commit
a closeout deploy or publication step is requested after merge or review
the target may already contain the approved artifact or data state

trigger_signals.description: The branch head contains commits beyond the reviewed or approved change range.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Do not use branch head as the release source without explicit release-candidate approval.

trigger_signals.description: The approved work may already be reflected in the live artifact or data ledger.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Verify containment first; a redeploy may promote unrelated head work.

trigger_signals.description: A deploy instruction names a feature, not a complete release candidate.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Construct the candidate from live plus approved changes or stop for release-scope clarification.

negative_signals.description: The reviewed artifact is itself the explicit release candidate and contains no unrelated commits.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then release and merge source may coincide for this operation.

negative_signals.description: The requester explicitly approved the advanced branch head as the release candidate.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then the scope is broader by decision, but still record the commit range.

common_wrong_assumptions: If a feature was reviewed, the current branch head is safe to deploy.
A closeout redeploy is harmless when the target already contains the fix.
Merged means authorized for every environment.

first_checks.check: Compare live commit/artifact, reviewed commit range, and current branch head.
first_checks.why: This reveals unrelated commits that would be promoted by a head deploy.

first_checks.check: If the target may already contain the approved work, verify artifact id, target commit, and ledger or migration status before redeploying.
first_checks.why: Already-live containment can make redeploy unnecessary and risky.

first_checks.check: Record excluded commits and candidate construction.
first_checks.why: Release evidence must show what did not ship as well as what did.

decision_rules.condition: Branch head includes work outside the approved change range.
decision_rules.then: Build or select a release candidate from live plus approved changes, or stop for explicit release-scope approval.

decision_rules.condition: Live artifact and data state already contain the approved work.
decision_rules.then: Record live artifact id, target commit, containment proof, ledger status, and excluded commits; do not redeploy unless required.

decision_rules.condition: The branch head is the approved release candidate.
decision_rules.then: Proceed through the normal release path with the exact commit range and review evidence.

do_not: Do not equate merge source with release source.
Do not redeploy just to “close out” if containment evidence proves the target already has the approved work.
Do not ship advanced branch-head work under a narrow feature approval.

Do not confuse this release-candidate scoping trap with moving-source-ref-during-long-deploy, where the ref moves during an in-flight deploy, or authorization-must-be-current-to-work-item, where stale approval is reused across work items.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before release, compare live, approved range, and branch head; deploy only the explicit release candidate or record already-live containment.

risk.notes: This record is de-identified agent guidance. It does not authorize bypassing maintainer, security, publication, production, billing, data, permission, or destructive-action gates.

title: Reproduce user-visible data bugs before asking the user to re-verify
summary: When a user reports that a data-backed UI still shows the wrong count, stale placement, or unchanged result after a fix, an agent may keep asking the user to click again instead of reproducing the exact data path. The safer pattern is to run the same read/query/apply/readback loop against representative data, then ask the user only for information the agent cannot observe.
ai_value: Reduces user frustration and catches mismatches between the intended model, the query predicate, and the rendered state. It also prevents agents from mistaking a successful unit test or code review for evidence that the operator-visible data path is fixed.

contexts: Data-backed admin or operator UIs
Rule engines, filters, labels, folders, queues, dashboards, and bulk actions
Bugs where the user's observable count, row placement, or detail view disagrees with the agent's expected state

trigger_signals.description: The user says a fixed rule still matches zero rows, the row remains in the old place, or the UI still shows stale labels/counts after applying the change.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Stop relying on the previous code-level check. Reproduce the exact user-visible data path and collect readback evidence.

trigger_signals.description: The implementation has separate preview, apply, receive-time, and detail/list queries that are supposed to share semantics.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Verify semantic parity across the paths rather than testing only one helper or endpoint.

negative_signals.description: The user-visible issue depends on credentials, live data, or privacy-sensitive facts the agent is not authorized to access.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not bypass access boundaries. Ask for the minimal missing observation or route through an approved debug path instead.

negative_signals.description: A deterministic local fixture reproduces the exact query/apply/render path and has already been run after the disputed fix.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A fixture can replace live-data readback when it covers the same predicates and state transitions.

common_wrong_assumptions: A passing unit test proves the operator-visible list is fixed.
If the helper function was corrected, preview, apply, receive-time, and detail views must all agree.
The user can cheaply verify one more time, so asking again is acceptable.
A zero-match result means there is no matching data, not that the query normalized the scope incorrectly.
A secondary label or stale relationship means the primary visible location is already correct.

first_checks.check: Identify the exact state the user expected to change: source predicate, destination/visible location, count, and the page or endpoint that displays it.
first_checks.why: Without the observable success state, the agent may verify a different path than the one the user is judging.

first_checks.check: Run a read-only count/readback query before mutation or against a fixture: source candidates, already-applied exclusions, and destination inventory.
first_checks.why: This separates no data, wrong scope normalization, and wrong already-applied predicates.

first_checks.check: After apply, re-read through the same data path the UI uses, not only through the helper that performed the write.
first_checks.why: Many bugs live in list/detail/read models rather than the write function.

first_checks.check: If asking the user again is unavoidable, include what the agent already verified and the one observation that remains inaccessible.
first_checks.why: This keeps the user from becoming the default test harness and makes the remaining gap explicit.

decision_rules.condition: The agent can access representative data or a faithful fixture safely.
decision_rules.then: Reproduce the failure with count/readback evidence, fix the predicate or state transition, and verify the same path after the change before asking for user confirmation.

decision_rules.condition: The path touches private live data or credentials outside the agent's grant.
decision_rules.then: Do not broaden access. Ask only for the smallest screenshot/count/log needed, or route through an authorized readback/debug workflow.

do_not: Do not ask the user to repeatedly test the same path while the agent has safe access to reproduce it.
Do not treat a helper-level unit test as proof that the rendered list, detail page, and counts agree.
Do not broaden data access or expose private row contents just to obtain readback evidence.
Do not publish real message subjects, account names, customer data, private URLs, tracker IDs, or tenant identifiers in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: For user-visible data bugs, write down the observable success state, then run a safe count/apply/readback loop against representative data before returning to the user.

risk.notes: The diagnostic pattern is safe when it stays read-only or uses authorized reversible test data. Live mutations, private data access, credentials, or irreversible actions still require the normal gate for that system.

sources.supports: A private agent session initially relied on code-level fixes and user retesting for a rule/list mismatch. The issue was resolved only after running representative apply/readback checks that exposed scope normalization and already-applied predicate bugs.

title: Resolve handoff identifiers against current state
summary: Identifiers in handoffs and design notes can go stale. Before attaching work, status, or tests to a task ID, migration filename, issue, or release number, resolve it against the current source of truth.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid filing evidence under the wrong anchor or following stale migration numbers after rebases and mainline movement.

contexts: a handoff names a task, issue, migration, release, artifact, branch, or other identifier
mainline advanced after a design note chose a numbered filename or slot
an agent is about to write status, tests, docs, or artifacts against a named identifier

trigger_signals.description: The handoff ID was provisional, old, or copied from a previous session.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Resolve it in the tracker or source before using it as the work anchor.

trigger_signals.description: A migration or numbered artifact was planned before rebasing or merging mainline.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Inspect the final directory and tests before recording the identifier.

negative_signals.description: The identifier is immutable and has been verified immediately before use.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Record the verification and proceed.

negative_signals.description: The identifier appears only as historical context, not as an execution anchor.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not over-process historical references.

common_wrong_assumptions: A named ID in a handoff is current because it was correct when written.
Migration numbers in design notes survive rebases unchanged.
If the title looks similar, the anchor must be the same work item.

first_checks.check: Resolve the ID in the authoritative current system before attaching artifacts.
first_checks.why: This prevents status or files from landing on the wrong work item.

first_checks.check: For numbered files or migrations, inspect the directory after rebasing and update tests/docs to the final name.
first_checks.why: The final merged identifier is what future agents will search for.

first_checks.check: Record rejected stale IDs when confusion is likely to recur.
first_checks.why: A note prevents the next agent from repeating the same stale-anchor mistake.

decision_rules.condition: A handoff identifier cannot be verified as the current target.
decision_rules.then: Resolve the current target or create the correct anchor through the normal workflow before writing artifacts or status.

decision_rules.condition: A final migration or numbered artifact differs from the design note.
decision_rules.then: Update handoff/tests/docs to the final merged identifier and preserve the stale number only as historical context.

do_not: Do not attach work to a task, issue, or migration number solely because a handoff named it.
Do not leave stale design-note identifiers as the only searchable clue.
Do not ask a human to choose between IDs until the agent has resolved current status and purpose.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Resolve every execution identifier against current state, then record the final ID and any rejected stale ID before handoff.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified. It does not authorize bypassing human, maintainer, security, publication, billing, data, or credential gates.

sources.excerpt: AI-session recovery guidance identified stale task anchors and default-mission drift as recurring sources of misplaced work.
sources.supports: Supports resolving handoff anchors before execution.

sources.excerpt: A migration filename can change after rebasing against main; future agents need the final merged identifier, not only the design-time number.
sources.supports: Supports final migration identifier recording.

title: Review artifacts need machine-checkable scope fields
summary: A high-risk review can look convincing but still be unusable by an automated gate when it lacks exact artifact identity, reviewer identity, role separation, reviewed/excluded scope, or fail-closed semantics.
ai_value: Adds a concrete field schema and review-only hard stop to the existing authorization lessons, without treating review evidence itself as landing authority.

contexts: code review, merge, migration, or deployment gates consume AI or peer review artifacts
the change is high-risk or platform policy requires independent review
a review-only worker could infer it should continue into merge/deploy after writing a verdict

trigger_signals.description: A gate rejects a review packet for missing head SHA, digest, reviewer identity, role separation, reviewed scope, or excluded scope.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The artifact is incomplete even if the prose says approved.

trigger_signals.description: A review artifact says approved but does not bind the approval to an exact commit or immutable artifact digest.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The approval cannot be safely matched to the thing being landed.

trigger_signals.description: A review-only worker reports success and then starts merging, deploying, applying migrations, or mutating live state.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The review-only stop condition was not machine-clear enough.

negative_signals.description: The change is low-risk, local-only, reversible, and project policy permits a lightweight self-check.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not import high-risk review ceremony into simple edits unnecessarily.

negative_signals.description: A separate platform gate has already converted the exact review artifact into formal approval for the current work item.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: This record covers artifact completeness and review-only stopping, not the authority cluster itself.

common_wrong_assumptions: A readable review verdict is enough for a machine gate.
Reviewer approval automatically grants merge or deploy authority.
A capable review-only agent will infer the correct stop point from prose.

first_checks.check: Require exact reviewed commit or immutable artifact digest, reviewer/provider identity, verdict, role separation, reviewed scope, excluded scope, and fail-closed meaning.
first_checks.why: These fields let gates and future agents verify what was actually reviewed.

first_checks.check: Dry-run the gate with each required field removed and confirm it fails closed.
first_checks.why: The schema must be machine-enforced, not merely documented.

first_checks.check: For review-only dispatches, assert the worker stops after producing the review artifact and does not run merge/deploy/live mutation commands.
first_checks.why: The stop condition needs behavioral evidence.

decision_rules.condition: A high-risk review artifact lacks exact artifact identity, reviewer identity, role separation, reviewed/excluded scope, or fail-closed semantics.
decision_rules.then: Do not consume it as gate evidence; request or generate a complete artifact bound to the exact artifact under review.

decision_rules.condition: A review-only agent is not explicitly barred from merge, deploy, live data, or irreversible mutation.
decision_rules.then: Add a hard stop to the briefing and wrapper: produce review artifact only, then return control.

do_not: Do not restate or bypass the existing rule that review evidence is not landing authority.
Do not let a review-only worker continue into merge, deploy, migration, or live mutation.
Do not accept a review artifact whose excluded scope is implicit.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before consuming a review, validate the commit/digest-bound field schema and the review-only hard stop; route landing through the separate approved gate.

title: Reviewers without git graph access need precomputed diff evidence
summary: A read-only reviewer can comment on visible files but cannot validate change range, ancestry direction, or merge-tree outcome unless the coordinator supplies computed git evidence.
ai_value: Helps agents match review packets to the reviewer's actual tool capability instead of mistaking file-read access for merge/release review scope.

contexts: a review-only AI or human has file-read access but cannot run git graph commands
the requested verdict depends on a branch range, ancestry, mergeability, or release artifact identity
a gate requires commit-bound evidence

trigger_signals.description: The reviewer reports it cannot compute git diff, merge-base, merge-tree, ancestry, or repository graph state.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Supply coordinator-computed evidence or narrow the review scope.

trigger_signals.description: The review prompt names source and target branches but omits exact base/head, diff, or merge simulation output.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The reviewer cannot validate the actual change range from prose alone.

trigger_signals.description: A gate asks for production, release, or merge approval but the reviewer sees only a working tree snapshot or selected files.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: File visibility is not graph visibility.

negative_signals.description: The task is a narrow semantic review of explicitly listed files and branch ancestry does not matter.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: File-read access can be sufficient when the decision does not depend on range or merge result.

negative_signals.description: A platform review UI already provides exact base/head, diff, and mergeability evidence to the reviewer.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The required evidence may already be present in another surface.

common_wrong_assumptions: If an AI can read local files, it can validate the same review scope as an agent with git commands.
A prose summary of changed files is enough for a merge gate.
Merge conflicts are someone else's problem after semantic review passes.

first_checks.check: Identify the reviewer's tool capability before requesting a diff, merge, release, or deployment-gate review.
first_checks.why: The packet must fill capability gaps.

first_checks.check: Attach exact base and head IDs, a three-dot diff or patch/stat, required ancestry checks, merge-tree or platform mergeability evidence, and explicit scope exclusions.
first_checks.why: These artifacts let a read-only reviewer make a range-bound judgment.

first_checks.check: Require the final review artifact to state which git-graph evidence was supplied or unavailable.
first_checks.why: The limitation must remain visible to the gate and future agents.

decision_rules.condition: The reviewer lacks git graph commands and the decision depends on range, ancestry, or mergeability.
decision_rules.then: Coordinator must provide base/head, diff, ancestry, mergeability, and exclusions before asking for approval.

decision_rules.condition: The reviewer receives only prose or selected files for a merge/release gate.
decision_rules.then: Treat the review as semantic-only or incomplete; do not consume it as merge safety evidence.

do_not: Do not pressure a restricted reviewer to infer merge safety from prose.
Do not call a semantic file review a graph/range review.
Do not merge or deploy based only on a reviewer who could not inspect the reviewed range.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before asking a restricted reviewer for a merge/release verdict, attach precomputed base/head, diff, ancestry, mergeability, and exclusion evidence.

title: Runtime secret preflight must use the workload identity
summary: A workload spec naming a secret does not prove the deployed workload identity can fetch it. Preflight secret access as the exact runtime identity before rollout.
ai_value: Helps agents catch rollout-only failures where build-time or operator credentials can read a secret but the platform runtime identity cannot.

contexts: a deployment adds or changes secrets, environment variables, or secret references
the platform fetches secrets using a runtime identity distinct from the operator or build identity
failure would appear only after rollout or task start

trigger_signals.description: The workload spec references a secret but no test uses the runtime identity that will fetch it.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Run or simulate secret retrieval as that exact identity before rollout.

trigger_signals.description: Operator or CI credentials can read the secret, but the deployed workload fails at startup.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Suspect runtime identity permissions rather than secret existence.

trigger_signals.description: Secret wiring is reviewed only by name, path, or environment variable presence.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Name matching is insufficient; verify the identity-resource permission edge.

negative_signals.description: The platform injects the secret at build time using the same identity that was tested.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The runtime-identity mismatch may not apply, but build/runtime exposure still needs review.

negative_signals.description: The secret is not fetched by the platform and is supplied through a separate verified channel.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Verify that channel instead of this workload-identity edge.

common_wrong_assumptions: If the secret name appears in the workload spec, rollout will be able to read it.
Operator credentials prove runtime permissions.
Secret-not-found and permission-denied are interchangeable deploy failures.

first_checks.check: Identify the exact runtime identity the platform uses to fetch secrets.
first_checks.why: It may differ from operator, CI, build, or application identities.

first_checks.check: Dry-run or simulate secret retrieval as that runtime identity before rollout.
first_checks.why: This catches permission failures before a live deployment attempt.

first_checks.check: Record both secret reference and permission edge in the rollout evidence.
first_checks.why: Names without identity evidence do not prove deployability.

decision_rules.condition: The runtime identity cannot be proven to read the referenced secret.
decision_rules.then: Do not roll out; repair or request the permission edge through the approved path.

decision_rules.condition: Operator credentials pass but runtime identity fails.
decision_rules.then: Treat this as a runtime permission edge failure, not a missing secret or application bug.

decision_rules.condition: The preflight passes as the exact workload identity.
decision_rules.then: Proceed with normal rollout checks while keeping secret values redacted.

do_not: Do not print secret values during preflight.
Do not infer runtime secret access from operator or CI access.
Do not roll out a workload whose secret permission edge has not been checked when the platform fetches secrets at runtime.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before rollout, identify the platform runtime identity and verify redacted secret access through that identity.

title: Preflight secondary runtime artifacts before reload
summary: A service config can validate while reload still fails because a secondary runtime artifact path such as a log, socket, cache, PID directory, or certificate store already exists with unsafe ownership or permissions.
ai_value: Helps infrastructure agents preflight the files a service opens at reload/start time, not only the primary config syntax, while keeping evidence-narrowing as a separate held topic.

contexts: deployment, reverse-proxy, or service automation validates configuration before reload
the service opens generated or pre-created runtime paths during reload/start
a secondary artifact can exist before the service creates it

trigger_signals.description: Config validation succeeds, but reload or start fails with a path, permission, ownership, or writability error.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The failing object may be a secondary runtime artifact, not the config file.

trigger_signals.description: The failed path is a log file, socket, cache, PID directory, certificate path, or similar runtime artifact.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Add runtime-path preflight to the reload checklist.

trigger_signals.description: The path already exists before reload with ownership the service account cannot write.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Fail closed before reload and fix through the approved maintenance path.

negative_signals.description: The service creates all runtime artifacts in a clean private directory and no pre-existing object can affect reload.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: An explicit filesystem preflight may be unnecessary when the service owns a clean artifact root.

negative_signals.description: The reload failure points to syntax, missing include, unavailable upstream, or another primary config error.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Diagnose primary config failures directly instead of applying this trap.

common_wrong_assumptions: Config-valid means reload-safe.
The only file that matters is the config file being validated.
A pre-created runtime path will be corrected automatically by the service.

first_checks.check: Extract every runtime path the service will open during reload/start and stat it before reload.
first_checks.why: Secondary artifacts can fail after syntax validation.

first_checks.check: Check expected owner, group, permissions, parent directory execute bits, and writability as the service account.
first_checks.why: Root-owned or stale artifacts can be invisible to config validators.

first_checks.check: Simulate a mis-owned runtime artifact in a disposable fixture and confirm preflight fails before reload.
first_checks.why: A fixture prevents the check from becoming documentation-only.

decision_rules.condition: A secondary runtime artifact exists with ownership or permissions the service cannot use.
decision_rules.then: Do not reload into failure; fix or recreate the artifact through the approved path, then rerun preflight and config validation.

decision_rules.condition: All secondary runtime artifacts are absent or writable as expected and config validation passes.
decision_rules.then: Proceed with the already-approved reload path and record preflight evidence.

do_not: Do not paste broad provider or infrastructure output into public/user-facing summaries as a substitute for focused preflight evidence.
Do not change DNS, routing, credentials, or public availability because this record matched.
Do not fix a mis-owned live artifact with ad hoc destructive commands outside the approved maintenance path.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before reload, preflight both primary config and secondary runtime paths as the service account; fail closed on unsafe pre-existing artifacts.
